st: Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb on all sides in batches and set it aside.
In the same pot, cook the onions for [[8 minutes]] until deep golden.
Add the garlic, cumin, cardamom, cinnamon stick and cloves and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook until thick and jammy.
Return the lamb to the pot, add [[2 cups]] hot water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the rice, the remaining [[2 cups]] hot water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat, cover tightly.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, remove the cinnamon, fluff with a fork and serve with banana and lime on the side.
Whisk the all-purpose flour, sorghum flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl.
Pour in [[2 cups]] warm water and whisk into a smooth, thin batter like crepe batter.
Cover and leave in a warm spot until bubbly and slightly sour smelling.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat and rub with a little oil.
Pour in about [[0.25 cup]] batter and tilt to spread into a round.
Cook on one side only, covered, until the surface is covered in tiny holes and set, with no browning on top, about 3 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and repeat. Serve warm with honey and butter or with stew.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the goat pieces for [[8 minutes]].
Add the onion, garlic and cumin and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water and add [[2 tsp]] salt and the chilies. Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook until the goat is tender.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer until soft.
Stir in the lime juice and half the cilantro. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the rest of the cilantro. Serve with flatbread.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet, add the onion and cook for [[4 minutes]] until soft.
Add the garlic, chili and ground beef. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned and no pink remains, reaching 160°F (71°C).
Stir in [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] salt and the cilantro. Cook until dry, then cool completely.
Stir [[2 tbsp]] flour and [[3 tbsp]] water into a thick glue for sealing.
Cut each wrapper strip, put a spoonful of filling at one end and fold over in triangles, like folding a flag, sealing the end with the glue.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the sambusas in batches until crisp and golden brown, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with hot sauce or lime.
Grease a 9-inch plate or a shallow dish with butter.
Whisk the cornstarch with [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until no lumps remain.
Bring [[3 cups]] water and the sugar to a boil in a heavy pot, stirring until dissolved.
Lower the heat and slowly pour in the cornstarch mixture while whisking constantly so it stays smooth.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring without stopping, until the mixture turns thick and glossy.
Add the butter a bit at a time, then the cardamom, nutmeg and rose water. Keep stirring until it pulls away from the pot.
Spread into the plate, top with nuts, and let it set for 2 hours before cutting.

ing: about 1 lb each, or fillets of firm white fish
st: Clean the fish, score each side three times, and rub with the lemon juice, [[1 tsp]] salt and half the garlic. Let sit 15 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onion for [[5 minutes]] until soft.
Add the remaining garlic, chili and [[1 tsp]] cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, [[0.5 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer until thick and saucy.
Pat the fish dry and coat lightly in the flour.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a large skillet to 350°F (175°C). Fry the fish for about [[4 minutes]] per side until golden and the flesh flakes easily.
Drain on paper towels, set on a platter and spoon the hot red sauce over the top.
